Denzel Curry.angle: lean into the technically dense, mosh-pit-energy flow angle -- aggressive delivery and lyrical density close to this song. Real corroboration: Alternative Press covers him in dedicated trap-metal coverage, and Album Of The Year also lists him in its roster

Rico Nasty.angle: lean into the aggressive, punk-infused trap angle -- covered by both Revolver (trap-metal crossover) and Consequence, and she's actually collaborated with City Morgue before, so the scene overlap here is real, not just a vibe comparison

Ho99o9.angle: lean into the punk/hardcore-crossover aggressive angle -- screamed hooks and mosh-oriented energy, close cousin to the trap-metal lineage. Covered by Revolver Magazine in the same trap-metal-crossover breath as Rico Nasty

nothing,nowhere..angle: lean into the screamed-hook, emo-trap crossover angle -- post-hardcore energy layered over rap verses, a close cousin to the Ghostemane/City Morgue lane. Covered by Alternative Press's dedicated trap-metal coverage, right alongside City Morgue

JPEGMAFIA.angle: lean into the abrasive, genre-blending aggressive hip-hop angle -- noisy production and confrontational delivery. Covered by Impose Magazine's alternative/indie lineup

Danny Brown.angle: lean into the frenetic, high-energy delivery angle -- an eccentric, aggressive flow that still leads with technical lyricism. Covered by Impose Magazine alongside JPEGMAFIA

Zombie Juice.angle: lean into the dark, horrorcore-tinged aggressive angle -- as a Flatbush Zombies member, his verses run gritty and technical. Covered by Beat Trotterz's underground hip-hop features

Freddie Gibbs.angle: lean into the gritty, technical lyricism angle -- dense, unflinching verses that carry weight without needing to shout. Covered by BBarak's underground hip-hop coverage
